note: Hulagu Khan sacks Baghdad (February 1258), executing the last Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim; the 500-year Abbasid Caliphate ends. The event is considered one of the most devastating in Islamic history; the House of Wisdom is destroyed and the irrigation systems of Mesopotamia irreparably damaged.

_quarry.structural_significance: Hülegü's destruction of Baghdad (1258) and execution of the last Abbasid caliph eliminated the symbolic centre of Sunni Islamic authority that had provided legitimacy for Islamic governance for five centuries; the psychological and political trauma reshaped Islamic political theory, while the Mamluk sultan's installation of a puppet Abbasid caliph in Cairo demonstrated both the caliphate's reduced importance and its continued ideological utility.
